og.title: Chrome Now Warns Before Insecure HTTP Connections
og.description: As promised last year, we have now rolled out a change where Chrome explicitly asks users for permission before making an insecure HTTP connection. Earlier this year we enabled this feature for users enrolled in Chrome's Enhanced Protection mode of Safe Browsing, and now we extended this protection to all users by default.

og.title: Protecting Chrome and Android Users from Compromised eMudhra Intermediate CA Certificates
og.description: The Chrome Root Program received a report from a security researcher regarding the compromise of private keys associated with eight eMudhra subordinate Certification Authority (CA) certificates. The team subsequently landed a CRLSet update blocking the Subject Public Key Info (SPKI) hashes of the affected intermediate CAs. Because this CRLSet update blocks by SPKI, Chrome users were immediately protected against all certificates sharing those keys, without requiring a browser update or restart.

og.title: Chrome's Response to Recent ccTLD Registry Hijacks
og.description: Following recent third-party domain hijacks affecting the .gh, .sl, and .as country-code top-level domains (ccTLDs), Chrome immediately blocked unauthorized HTTPS certificates via CRLSets and worked with issuing Certification Authorities to revoke them. Using Certificate Transparency (CT) logs, Chrome also proactively identified and blocked certificates for other impacted organizations. While Chrome users are automatically protected without needing to take action, we strongly encourage domain owners to monitor CT logs across their entire domain portfolio and publish restrictive CAA records to safeguard their namespaces.
